```{python}
#| label: fig-wdep-phis
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Depletion width $W_\\mathrm{dep}$ (left) and surface potential $\\Phi_\\mathrm{S}$ (right) as a function of the gate potential $V_\\mathrm{G}$, calculated with the depletion approximation for $N_\\mathrm{a} = 3 \\times 10^{18}\\,\\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$, $t_\\mathrm{ox} = 2\\,$nm, and $\\Phi_\\mathrm{fb} = -1.05\\,$V. Once inversion is reached at $\\Phi_\\mathrm{S} = 2\\Phi_\\mathrm{B}$ (at $V_\\mathrm{G} = V_\\mathrm{th} \\approx 0.5\\,$V), both quantities saturate."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

q = 1.602e-19
eps_si = 11.9 * 8.854e-12       # F/m
Na = 3e18 * 1e6                 # 1/m^3
Cox = 17.3e-3                   # F/m^2 (17.3 fF/um^2)
phi_b = 0.50                    # V
phi_fb = -1.05                  # V

# depletion approximation: VG = phi_fb + q Na W^2/(2 eps_si) + q Na W / Cox
a = q * Na / (2 * eps_si)
b = q * Na / Cox

vg = np.linspace(phi_fb, 1.5, 400)
wdep = (-b + np.sqrt(b**2 + 4 * a * (vg - phi_fb))) / (2 * a)
wdep = np.clip(wdep, 0, None)

# beyond inversion the depletion width saturates at its maximum value
wdep_max = np.sqrt(2 * eps_si * 2 * phi_b / (q * Na))
wdep = np.minimum(wdep, wdep_max)
phi_s = np.minimum(a * wdep**2, 2 * phi_b)

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.4))

axs[0].plot(vg, wdep / 1e-9, 'b-', lw=2)
axs[0].set_xlabel('$V_\\mathrm{G}$ (V)')
axs[0].set_ylabel('$W_\\mathrm{dep}$ (nm)')
axs[0].grid(alpha=0.3)

axs[1].plot(vg, phi_s, 'b-', lw=2)
axs[1].axhline(2 * phi_b, color='gray', ls=':', lw=1)
axs[1].text(-1.0, 2 * phi_b + 0.05, '$2\\Phi_\\mathrm{B}$', fontsize=9)
axs[1].set_xlabel('$V_\\mathrm{G}$ (V)')
axs[1].set_ylabel('$\\Phi_\\mathrm{S}$ (V)')
axs[1].set_ylim(-0.1, 1.5)
axs[1].grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
